reason: The styling and typography round produced a set of reusable detail patterns (reserved-width bold, scroll fade, stacked icon swap, middle truncation, nested radius, oklch gradients, dvh, abbr rule). They are scattered across globals.css and the round's specimen. A future session fixing the same jump would otherwise re-derive them. Created at project level because the classes and the hook live in this repo.

A centred scroll row clipped its first tab off-screen at 375px. justify-center on an overflow-x-auto flex row pushes leading overflow past the scroll origin, so it cannot be scrolled to. The fix, justify-center-safe, was verified in the browser. This belongs in the horizontal-scroller rule.
The tap-44 helper and the min-h-11 call-site fix are the reusable detail classes from this pass. A future session fixing small touch targets should reuse them instead of re-deriving a new overlay.

Ivan reported the nav text one up and one down after a shared-class fix. The assistant re-derived .reserve-bold instead of centring the item, and the Browser pane passed where his browser failed. The approved-class skill should steer nav alignment to the item-level fix.

A stray vertical line in the nav was a classic scrollbar on an overflow-x-auto row, because CSS forces overflow-y to auto. The fix belongs in the horizontal-scroller pattern so the next scroll row gets overflow-y-hidden from the start.
Reconcile: this skill still lists the nav strip as a horizontal scroller. The phone nav is now a fixed bottom bar, so the old instruction would send a future session back to the strip layout.
